<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/automation.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **145** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a3f82efa7d588267eb2e52c06a73c56315c636a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `70790eb170e4c3088b6ed0b9f5decb42229f58b7` — the merge of head `63f2467e48d0b5a9d450d8eb3ae6ebcb8c4e0669` into base `6a3f82efa7d588267eb2e52c06a73c56315c636a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 70790eb170e4c3088b6ed0b9f5decb42229f58b7 && git checkout 70790eb170e4c3088b6ed0b9f5decb42229f58b7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6a3f82efa7d588267eb2e52c06a73c56315c636a 63f2467e48d0b5a9d450d8eb3ae6ebcb8c4e0669 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6a3f82efa7d588267eb2e52c06a73c56315c636a && git merge --no-ff 63f2467e48d0b5a9d450d8eb3ae6ebcb8c4e0669

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a3f82efa7d588267eb2e52c06a73c56315c636a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6a3f82efa7d588267eb2e52c06a73c56315c636a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `63f2467e48d0b5a9d450d8eb3ae6ebcb8c4e0669`
Local-runs: none

Rendered 2026-10-10T01:01Z on the read-only shape: card #22507 (body and all eight comments), PR #22555 (body, the 27-file list, and the net diff against the merge base 4638625e0 — file list and diff agree at +1592/−97), and the check-runs on the head. The head's parent is the merge of `origin/main` at 4638625e0; `main` has since moved (6a3f82efa) and only the PR's own delta is judged. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.

1. **Right — `flows.FLOW.successMessage` / `.errorMessage` join the face** (`translation.zod.ts`), replacing the guidance refusal. `translateFlow` overlays a toast only where `typeof flow[key] === 'string'`, so a bundle cannot add one, and a flow nothing resolves comes back as the same reference. The engine carries both strings verbatim on the terminal result (`engine.ts` at the merge base: `successMessage: flow.successMessage`, `errorMessage: flow.errorMessage`), so the client-side overlay is the right route — the one `label` already takes. The four new aliases (`success`, `successText`, `error`, `errorText`) refuse with a rename, not a tolerance.
2. **Right — `…fields.FIELD.options.VALUE` joins the field face** as a string-to-string record keyed by `String(value)` through one new function, `flowScreenFieldOptionKey`, read by the schema refusal, `translateFlow`, `resolveFlowScreenFieldOptions`, the lint and the extractor alike. Not by position (a reorder would re-point every translation); not from an object field (a screen field declares no such binding). `options` is deliberately NOT in `FLOW_SCREEN_FIELD_COPY_KEYS` (a map over an array, not a string key), and the lookup reads own keys only. The aliases `choices` / `values` refuse with a rename. The key is the console select's own identity for an option (`ScreenView.tsx` at the objectui pin f0268ad78 keys each `SelectItem` by `String(o.value)`).
3. **Right — the one accept-set narrowing.** `ScreenFieldConfigSchema` now refuses two options of one field whose values read the same as text, at the second option's `value`, leading with `SCREEN_FIELD_OPTION_VALUE_COLLISION`, naming both options by position and value, closing with the remedy; the refusal reaches the `FlowSchema` door. Reach measured 0 over the in-repo examples at 37c711449 (35 flows / 6 screens / 2 option fields / 10 options); hotcrm and hotclm by inspection, declared as inspection.
4. **Right — the exclusion texts.** `FLOW_SCREEN_FIELD_NO_OPTIONS` is deleted with no leftover reference at the head; the toast guidance is gone; the screen `description` guidance now says "has no key … yet", why (the server renders it per run), and what the face does carry. `BULK_PARAM_NO_OPTIONS` keeps its own measured exclusion and says this change did not touch it.
5. **Right — public surface, additive.** `@objectstack/spec` gains `SCREEN_FIELD_OPTION_VALUE_COLLISION` and `flowScreenFieldOptionKey` (automation), `FLOW_TERMINAL_MESSAGE_KEYS`, `FlowTerminalMessageKey`, `FlowScreenFieldOptionLike` and `resolveFlowScreenFieldOptions` (system); `FlowLike` and `FlowScreenFieldLike` gain optional members. `api-surface/` and `export-origins/` carry each one in the diff.
6. **Right — `@objectstack/lint`.** A toast over a flow that declares none is `translation-target-unknown` (error, the orphan rule); an option key naming no declared value, naming a label, or sitting under a field that declares no `options` is `translation-option-key-unknown` (warning) — the rule and severity of the object-field and action-param legs — judged against the field's own `options[]` read through the same key function, never an object field's options.
7. **Right — `@objectstack/cli`.** The extractor scaffolds exactly the keys the resolver reads (option keys through the same function); the coverage gate demands `errorMessage` for every flow that authors one and `successMessage` only for a flow with a screen. Both predicates mirror the readers at the objectui pin: `FlowRunner.tsx:439` draws `outcome.successMessage` in the screen runner alone; `flowResponse.ts:217` prefers `data.errorMessage` for any failed run.
8. **Right — the family pin** `flows-translation-face.test.ts` walks the flow schemas mechanically, classifies every text-bearing leaf as `keyed` / `noReader` / `elsewhere` / `owed`, pins the `owed` set exactly (`screen.description`, `approval.decisionOutputs[].label`), fails on a stale row and on a face key no slot fills. The reported ablation (a planted `subtitle`, a renamed face key — red, then restored blob == HEAD) is the dev's reading; the pin's own green is CI's to confirm (Test Core, pending below).
9. **Right — the ledger.** Two new child rows, `flows.successMessage` / `flows.errorMessage`, are `planned` with their reader named (contract-first, the shape `screens` took); the container stays `live`; the option map stays inside the `screens` row by the one-drill-level boundary; state counts 27 live / 2 planned / 29 classified. `Spec property liveness` is green on the head.
10. **Right, and declared — files beyond the claim's surface:** `builtin-node-config.zod.ts` (the home of the refusal the claim orders), the new key leaf and its barrel line, the regenerated `builtin-node-config.mdx`, and three example bundles translated so `check:i18n-coverage` holds at its baseline rather than widening the ratchet. Each mechanical or implied by the claim; the report declared each.
11. **Right — the references** under `content/docs/references/` are regenerated through the generator, not hand-edited; the refusal prose, the guidance and the lint messages carry no tracker number.

No governed path in the 27 files; head repo equals base repo; about 1,689 changed lines (under the 5,000 line and the 3,000 line).

### ② Semver level

- The `Clause-②` declaration reads `yes (narrowing)` on both carriers — the changeset and the PR body's line 2 — and that is what the diff publishes: a widening (new face keys, new exports) AND an accept-set narrowing (item 3). The earlier spelling, which hid the narrowing from `check-adr-0087-registration`, was corrected in fix round 1 (`6091764200`); that correction is the only change in `63f2467e4` (+6/−2 on the changeset, no source).
- Levels `minor` for `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/cli` — right: the launch-window grade for a breaking change, and at least `minor` for the two additive packages.
- The changeset carries the BREAKING banner naming the narrowing, the remedy (give each option a value that stays distinct as text, or drop the duplicate), the measured reach, and the one ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — honest: nothing is removed, renamed or re-shaped, so `objectstack migrate meta` has no rewrite and no mapping applies; the refusal carries the fix at every door that parses a flow.
- `Check Changeset` (`check-empty-changeset`, `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-changeset-no-major`) is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

Each dev flag and `open_questions` entry, answered or escalated.

- **Q1 — which reader picks a screen's translated `description`: ESCALATED to the maintainer, deliberately not answered here** (seat `6091764200`, `6091840731`). The server-render claim holds at the merge base: `service-automation/src/builtin/screen-nodes.ts` serves `description: text(cfg.description)` through `renderTextSlot`, flat and object-form screens alike, so an overlay on the served string would draw a translated hole literally. Leaving the slot `owed` is recorded honestly in every carrier: the face's TSDoc ("Not keyed: a screen's `description` … owed, not excluded … a decision of its own, not taken here"), the runtime guidance ("has no key … yet … no reader does that today"), the pin's `owed` row naming the decision it waits on, the `i18n-resolver.ts` docblock, the ledger container note, the changeset's "Still not keyed" bullet, and the PR body. One nit, not blocking: the older sentence in the ledger's `screens` row ("stay untranslated here by ruling") now reads against the owed framing; the PR that routes `description` rewrites it when it edits that row.
- **Q2 — the `Clause-②` spelling: answered B, done** (verified in ②).
- **Q3 — the first line: answered A, `Part of #22507`**; `Part-of PR must not also close its card` is green; the card stays open for the owed rows.
- **`approval.decisionOutputs[].label` recorded `owed`** — outside the triage enumeration, pinned, held on this card by the seat as remaining work. ESCALATED beside Q1: the maintainer's decision act on #22507 should also say whether it stays on this card or becomes its own; the pin's `OWED` list is edited in the same PR that routes it.
- **`BULK_PARAM_NO_OPTIONS`, and action-param inline options keyed by `String(value)` with no collision refusal** — declared in the Acceptance notes, not this card; noted as a convention asymmetry across the three option maps, for a follow-up card if the maintainer wants one convention.
- **The objectui runner card** (three reads: `resolveFlowScreenFieldOptions` in `localizeScreen`, `successMessage` in the success toast, `errorMessage` in `flowFailureMessage` through both launch hosts) — named in the PR body; the two `planned` rows flip when it lands at a pin. Two items go into that card: the runner's header note at the pin ("`FlowSchema.successMessage` — off the translation surface by design", `FlowRunner.tsx:117`) is stale, and `ScreenView` submits `String(value)` for a select.
- **`check:platform-checklist`** is red on `main` itself (#22557), kept out of per-PR CI; not this diff.
